rationale: Provider Dialect subclasses require a supported constructor accepting an explicitly chosen database version.
notes: Constructor support is explicit and independent of type-level roles.

rationale: Provider Dialect subclasses require a supported constructor accepting database metadata discovered during Dialect resolution.
notes: Constructor support is explicit and independent of type-level roles.

rationale: Provider Dialects override this focused database rendering hook and may delegate unhandled cast combinations to the inherited implementation.
notes: The focused rendering hook remains on Dialect; it does not select a full SQM translator.

rationale: Provider Dialects override this hook to supply the multi-table insert strategy required by their database capabilities.
notes: Its reachable signature must contain only supported API or SPI.

rationale: Provider Dialects override this hook to supply the multi-table mutation strategy required by their database capabilities.
notes: Its reachable signature must contain only supported API or SPI.

rationale: HQL parsing and translator selection are global query-engine integration concerns rather than database Dialect behavior.
replacement: QueryEngineOptions global HQL translator integration
notes: Direct removal without deprecation was approved; a versioned Migration Guide entry is mandatory.

rationale: Provider Dialects override this focused hook for database-specific set-operator rendering and may delegate standard operators to the inherited implementation.
notes: This is focused database rendering rather than full SQM translator selection.

rationale: Provider Dialects supply the SQL AST translator factory used to construct their database-specific translators.
notes: The factory and its complete request and result boundaries require focused review before classification is applied.

rationale: Database-local syntax variation should use focused capabilities; general SQM translator selection belongs to query-engine integration rather than Dialect.
replacement: Focused Dialect capabilities or QueryEngineOptions global SQM translator integration
notes: Direct removal without deprecation was approved; a versioned Migration Guide entry is mandatory.

rationale: Provider Dialects override this focused database rendering hook and may delegate supported trim forms to the inherited implementation.
notes: The focused rendering hook remains on Dialect; it does not select a full SQM translator.

rationale: Provider Dialect subclasses may select Hibernate's documented legacy LOB merge policy without reimplementing it.
notes: Protected policy constant intentionally available to Dialect implementors; no in-repository field access was observed.

rationale: Provider Dialect subclasses may select Hibernate's documented new-locator LOB merge policy without reimplementing it.
notes: Protected policy constant intentionally available to Dialect implementors; the inherited getter uses it by default.

rationale: Provider Dialect subclasses may reuse Hibernate's standard parameter-limit-aware multi-key sizing policy without reimplementing it.
notes: Protected policy constant intentionally available to Dialect implementors; the inherited multi-key sizing getter uses it by default.

rationale: Provider Dialect subclasses may select Hibernate's documented stream-transfer LOB merge policy without reimplementing it.
notes: Protected policy constant intentionally available to Dialect implementors; no in-repository field access was observed.

rationale: Provider Dialects may supply the key-sizing policy Hibernate uses for batch-fetch loading.
notes: No in-repository override was observed, but the method is a documented focused strategy hook and delegates to multi-key sizing by default.

rationale: Provider Dialects may supply the LOB merge policy consumed by Hibernate's JDBC LOB handling.
notes: The default returns NEW_LOCATOR_LOB_MERGE_STRATEGY; Hibernate has three direct consumers.

rationale: Provider Dialects may supply the key-sizing policy Hibernate uses for multi-id and multi-natural-id loading.
notes: No in-repository override was observed, but the method is a documented focused strategy hook and Hibernate has direct consumers.

rationale: Provider Dialects supply database-specific column size resolution used throughout Hibernate's type and schema machinery.
notes: Eight in-repository overrides and ten direct consumers were observed; change the retained method's result to the supported top-level SizeStrategy introduced by the Phase 5 type-family remediation.

rationale: Provider Dialects override this focused builder to supply a database-specific locking-clause strategy and may delegate to the inherited standard implementation.
notes: Three overrides and provider super-delegation were observed; PessimisticLockKind must move to a supported boundary before this SPI commitment is applied.

rationale: Provider Dialects select or construct the locking-clause strategy Hibernate uses for a specific SQL AST query and may delegate supported cases to the inherited implementation.
notes: Eight overrides were observed; QuerySpec and the complete LockingClauseStrategy boundary must be supported as part of the SQL AST migration.

rationale: Provider Dialects supply the composed metadata and operations describing their pessimistic-locking support.
notes: Forty-five overrides were observed; LockingSupport and provider-facing composition or construction facilities must avoid reliance on org.hibernate.dialect.lock.internal.

rationale: The deprecated Dialect-level getter duplicates the read-row strategy now supplied through LockingSupport.Metadata.
replacement: getLockingSupport().getMetadata().getReadRowLockStrategy()
notes: Migrate internal and provider overrides before direct removal and add a versioned Migration Guide entry.

rationale: The deprecated Dialect-level getter duplicates the write-row strategy now supplied through LockingSupport.Metadata.
replacement: getLockingSupport().getMetadata().getWriteRowLockStrategy()
notes: Migrate the remaining community override and internal consumers before direct removal and add a versioned Migration Guide entry.

rationale: Provider Dialects supply the global temporary-table behavior Hibernate uses when that independently supported kind is selected.
notes: A null result means unsupported; fourteen overrides were observed and the strategy boundary must contain only supported types.

rationale: Provider Dialects supply the local temporary-table behavior Hibernate uses when that independently supported kind is selected.
notes: A null result means unsupported; twenty overrides were observed and the strategy boundary must contain only supported types.

rationale: Provider Dialects may replace the inherited persistent-table fallback with database-specific naming, DDL, and lifecycle behavior.
notes: The inherited result is non-null; retain composition as the default path instead of requiring a supported persistent subclass base.

rationale: A single supported-kind value cannot represent Dialects which independently support multiple temporary-table strategies.
replacement: getLocalTemporaryTableStrategy(), getGlobalTemporaryTableStrategy(), getPersistentTemporaryTableStrategy(), and TemporaryTableStrategy#getTemporaryTableKind()
notes: Deprecated for removal since 7.1; migrate twenty-one overrides and remove LegacyTemporaryTableStrategy with the related legacy Dialect methods and a versioned Migration Guide entry.

rationale: Provider Dialects supply their identity-column DDL and generated-value behavior and may delegate version-dependent cases to the inherited support.
notes: Forty overrides and provider super-delegation were observed; move the feature contracts to identity.spi and replace the concrete GetGeneratedKeysDelegate signature with a supported generated-values boundary.

rationale: The deprecated string-based hook serves only deprecated legacy generator interpretation and duplicates the typed native value-generation strategy.
replacement: getNativeValueGenerationStrategy()
notes: Deprecated for removal since 7.0; migrate the one community override and legacy internal callers and add a versioned Migration Guide entry.

rationale: Provider Dialects supply the typed Jakarta generation strategy used when native identifier generation is requested.
notes: Nine overrides were observed; the Jakarta GenerationType return keeps the boundary small and supported.

rationale: Provider Dialects supply the database's DML-target qualification policy, and provider SQL AST translators consume that policy while rendering mutation statements.
notes: Twenty-nine overrides and provider-side SQL AST translator calls were observed; DmlTargetColumnQualifierSupport is a focused value type which must be classified as USE SPI.

rationale: Provider Dialects supply how GROUP BY clauses reference select items, and provider SQL AST translators consume that policy while rendering queries.
notes: Ten overrides and provider-side SQL AST translator calls were observed; SelectItemReferenceStrategy is a focused value type which must be classified as USE SPI.

rationale: Provider Dialects supply supported catalog and schema qualification, and may consume the inherited result while configuring provider-specific identifier helpers.
notes: Eighteen overrides and provider-side use were observed; the return type is already in an .spi package.

rationale: Provider Dialects supply nationalized-character handling and may delegate version- or driver-independent cases to the inherited policy.
notes: Fifteen overrides and provider super-delegation were observed; NationalizationSupport is a focused value type which must be classified as USE SPI.

rationale: Provider Dialects may supply a native JDBC parameter-marker renderer and may reuse the inherited standard-marker choice when selecting a driver-specific policy.
notes: Two overrides and provider super-use were observed; null means use Hibernate's standard marker and ParameterMarkerStrategy already resides in org.hibernate.sql.ast.spi.

rationale: Provider Dialects supply the database-specific temporal-table capability, DDL, and query-rendering policy consumed by Hibernate.
notes: Seven overrides and sixteen consumers were observed; move the contract to temporal.spi and replace mutable boot/model signature types with supported request or context views before applying the SPI commitment.

rationale: Provider Dialects supply the database's native time-zone type capability used by mapping and JDBC type selection.
notes: Seventeen overrides and three direct consumers were observed; TimeZoneSupport is a focused value type which must be included in the supported signature boundary.

rationale: Provider Dialects customize optional-table mutation construction and may delegate cases requiring Hibernate's standard update-then-insert behavior to the inherited implementation.
replacement: A supported optional-table mutation creation boundary using the semantic model-mutation SPI and supported result-construction facilities
notes: Twelve overrides and provider super-delegation were observed; remove the internal OptionalTableUpdate and transitional EntityMutationTarget types from the signature and present the exact replacement request or context and result-construction shape for focused review.

rationale: Provider Dialects supply the aggregate-column DDL, mapping, and SQL-expression behavior consumed by Hibernate.
notes: Twenty-three overrides were observed; move the coherent contract to aggregate.spi, audit its mapping and SQL AST signatures, and provide supported family factories, bases, composition, or an appropriate combination without classifying built-in leaves wholesale.

rationale: Provider Dialects supply procedure-call interpretation and parameter-registration behavior consumed by Hibernate.
notes: Thirteen overrides were observed; CallableStatementSupport is already in .spi, but providers currently depend on internal standard and vendor implementations, so expose a supported standard family base or composable equivalent while retaining internal built-in leaves.

rationale: Provider Dialects supply the immutable minimum database version used for version fallback and compatibility diagnostics without expanding every supported constructor and family-constructor signature.
notes: Nineteen overrides were observed and every one returns a constant; document that the hook is invoked during superclass construction and must return construction-safe immutable data without depending on subclass initialization.

rationale: Provider Dialects supply whether Hibernate may create and drop schema namespaces during schema management.
notes: Thirteen overrides and three direct schema-management consumers were observed; the boolean boundary is already compact and supported.

rationale: Provider Dialects supply the database-specific SQL commands Hibernate executes to create a schema namespace.
notes: Seven overrides and two direct schema-management consumers were observed; the String input and String-array result form a small supported boundary.

rationale: Current-schema discovery is provided by Connection#getSchema() or a custom SchemaNameResolver, and Hibernate no longer consumes this deprecated SQL-command hook.
replacement: Connection#getSchema() or getSchemaNameResolver()
notes: Deprecated since 7.0; thirteen overrides remain but the only call site is provider-owned resolver code, so migrate in-repository overrides and add a versioned Migration Guide entry before removal.

rationale: Provider Dialects supply schema-drop SQL and may delegate standard cases to the inherited command rendering.
notes: Twelve overrides, a direct schema-management consumer, and provider super-delegation were observed; the String input and String-array result form a small supported boundary.

rationale: Provider Dialects supply whether the inherited schema-drop renderer may use IF EXISTS.
notes: Six overrides were observed; Hibernate consumes the focused capability through the inherited getDropSchemaCommand implementation.

rationale: Provider Dialects supply whether the inherited schema-create renderer may use IF NOT EXISTS.
notes: Five overrides were observed; Hibernate consumes the focused capability through the inherited getCreateSchemaCommand implementation.

rationale: The sequence-discovery SQL is configuration of a SequenceInformationExtractor rather than an independent Dialect capability, and retaining both hooks creates a callback dependency between the extractor and Dialect.
replacement: getSequenceInformationExtractor() returning a supported standard extractor configured with its lookup SQL and result-column mapping
notes: Thirty-six overrides were observed; migrate them with the extractor implementations, eliminate extractor callbacks to Dialect#getQuerySequencesString, and add a versioned Migration Guide entry.

rationale: Provider Dialects supply sequence DDL export behavior and may delegate supported cases to Hibernate's inherited standard exporter.
notes: Three overrides, three consumers, and provider super-delegation were observed; Exporter already resides in schema.spi, while StandardSequenceExporter needs a supported family base or composable name-formatting variation point.

rationale: Provider Dialects supply sequence metadata extraction and may delegate unsupported or version-dependent cases to the inherited extractor selection.
notes: Twenty-three overrides and provider super-delegation were observed; retain SequenceInformationExtractor in schema extraction SPI and replace provider dependencies on internal legacy and no-op implementations with supported bases, builders, strategies, or constants.

rationale: Provider Dialects supply sequence DDL and value-retrieval semantics and may inspect or delegate to inherited sequence support when selecting a version-dependent strategy.
notes: Forty overrides, provider calls, and provider super-delegation were observed; move the coherent feature contract to sequence.spi and expose only justified standard or family bases while keeping built-in leaves internal.

rationale: Schema-management tool selection is a global service integration concern already handled by explicit configuration and Java service loading, not database-specific Dialect behavior.
replacement: hibernate.schema_management_tool, Java service loading for SchemaManagementTool, or normal service-registry integration
notes: Incubating with no observed overrides; make HibernateSchemaManagementTool the initiator default after configured and service-loaded choices and add a versioned Migration Guide entry for direct removal.

rationale: Provider Dialects supply database-specific JDBC or metadata-schema extraction behavior to Hibernate's schema-management tooling.
notes: Nine overrides and one schema-tool consumer were observed; the input and result already reside in extraction SPI, but providers need supported JDBC-metadata bases, strategies, or composition instead of internal extractor implementations.

rationale: Provider Dialects supply database- or driver-specific current-schema resolution when Connection#getSchema() is insufficient.
notes: Three overrides and one consumer were observed; SchemaNameResolver already resides in jdbc.env.spi and its functional interface supports direct provider implementations without internal dependencies.

rationale: All Dialects use NONE, so an overridable transaction-handling hook and its enum add unsupported surface without representing any database variation.
replacement: Unconditional non-isolated temporary-table DDL execution
notes: Deprecated since 7.0 with no observed overrides; simplify the two internal consumers, remove TempTableDdlTransactionHandling, and add a versioned Migration Guide entry.

rationale: A recent Oracle-only fixed-delay workaround controlling Hibernate's schema executor is not a coherent database capability or a supportable provider contract.
replacement: Resolve the Oracle temporal-DDL requirement or encapsulate any still-required coordination in internal schema execution
notes: Introduced as an Incubating deprecated-for-removal TODO with one Oracle override and one internal consumer; remove it outright if the underlying issue is resolved, otherwise keep the workaround internal and do not establish a Migration Guide contract for an unreleased temporary hook.

rationale: The generic TypeContributor bridge duplicates the focused Dialect type-contribution hook and unnecessarily presents a Dialect as an independently selectable application TypeContributor.
replacement: contributeTypes(TypeContributions, ServiceRegistry)
notes: Two HANA-family overrides and three calls were observed; move their early configuration into contributeTypes, have bootstrap call that focused hook directly, remove TypeContributor from Dialect, and add a versioned Migration Guide entry.

rationale: The generic FunctionContributor bridge is unused because query-engine bootstrap already invokes the focused Dialect function-registry hook directly.
replacement: initializeFunctionRegistry(FunctionContributions)
notes: No overrides or call sites were observed; remove FunctionContributor from Dialect and add a versioned Migration Guide entry distinguishing Dialect function customization from independently registered FunctionContributor services.

rationale: Provider Dialects contribute database-specific JDBC, DDL, and basic type descriptors and may invoke the inherited contribution before adding family- or database-specific descriptors.
notes: Thirty-three overrides and extensive provider super-delegation were observed; retain this as the single general Dialect type-contribution hook with TypeContributions and ServiceRegistry in its supported boundary.

rationale: Provider Dialects contribute database-specific HQL and SQL function descriptors and may invoke the inherited standard registrations before adding or replacing functions.
notes: Fifty overrides and extensive provider super-delegation were observed; retain this as the single Dialect function-contribution hook with FunctionContributions in its supported boundary.

rationale: Provider Dialects contribute database-specific DDL type descriptors and may invoke the inherited ANSI-oriented registrations before replacing or extending them.
notes: Thirty overrides and extensive provider super-delegation were observed; retain this focused protected sub-hook beneath contributeTypes and ensure the DDL type registry operations used by providers are supported.

rationale: Dialect contribution order is fixed by Hibernate bootstrap and the inherited contributor ordinal has no meaning after Dialect no longer implements TypeContributor or FunctionContributor.
replacement: No replacement; independent TypeContributor and FunctionContributor implementations retain their own ordinal contracts
notes: No overrides or direct calls were observed; remove the method with the generic contributor interfaces and document the separation in the Migration Guide.

rationale: Provider Dialects may render nonstandard array literals while reusing Hibernate's inherited ANSI ARRAY syntax where applicable.
notes: No in-repository overrides and one literal-formatter consumer were observed; retain the focused hook and ensure SqlAppender, JdbcLiteralFormatter, and WrapperOptions are supported for provider invocation.

rationale: Provider Dialects render java.time temporal literals using database-specific syntax and may delegate supported temporal forms to the inherited JDBC-escape rendering.
notes: Twenty-six overrides, four consumers, and provider super-delegation were observed; retain this independently invoked representation-specific overload and its supported rendering boundary.

rationale: Provider Dialects render Calendar literals using database-specific syntax and may delegate supported temporal forms to the inherited JDBC-escape rendering.
notes: Nineteen overrides, one consumer, and provider super-delegation were observed; retain this independently invoked representation-specific overload because Calendar time-zone semantics are not equivalent to simple java.time conversion.

rationale: Provider Dialects render legacy Date literals using database-specific syntax and may delegate supported temporal forms to the inherited JDBC-escape rendering.
notes: Twenty-three overrides, two consumers, and provider super-delegation were observed; retain this independently invoked representation-specific overload while legacy Date mappings remain supported.

rationale: Provider Dialects define cast-target type names which differ from column declarations and may delegate unchanged JDBC type codes to inherited type rendering.
notes: Fourteen overrides, thirteen consumers, and extensive provider super-delegation were observed; retain the focused protected hook and document supported SqlTypes codes and placeholder semantics.

rationale: Provider Dialects define database column type names for JDBC and extended SqlTypes codes and may delegate unchanged codes to inherited ANSI-oriented rendering.
notes: Forty-three overrides, forty-two consumers, and extensive provider super-delegation were observed; retain this foundational protected hook with explicit supported type-code and placeholder semantics.

rationale: Provider Dialects define standard, named, or otherwise database-specific array type names and may delegate standard element types to inherited ANSI rendering.
notes: Four overrides, seven consumers, and provider super-delegation were observed; retain the focused hook and document nullability and the distinct Java-element, SQL-element, and maximum-length inputs.

rationale: The JDBC-type-code overload cannot express size or named and aggregate type information and is superseded by the mapping-aware overload.
replacement: getSelectClauseNullString(SqlTypedMapping, TypeConfiguration)
notes: Deprecated for removal with thirteen overrides and two consumers; migrate all overrides and callers to the mapping-aware hook and add a versioned Migration Guide entry.

rationale: Provider Dialects render typed null expressions for union queries using complete SQL mapping information and may delegate mappings requiring no special cast to inherited rendering.
notes: Two overrides and two consumers were observed; make this the sole typed-null hook and ensure SqlTypedMapping and the required TypeConfiguration operations are in the supported provider boundary.

rationale: Provider Dialects define cast-target type names for positions such as set-returning-function declarations where LOB type names are not accepted, while delegating other codes to inherited rendering.
notes: One override, two consumers, and provider super-delegation were observed; retain the focused Incubating hook because its semantic constraint differs from general castType rendering.

rationale: Provider Dialects refine JDBC and extended SqlTypes equivalence for schema validation and migration while delegating unmatched type pairs to the inherited compatibility rules.
notes: Three overrides and three direct consumers were observed; document the accepted type-code domain and the directional compatibility semantics used by the inherited implementation.

rationale: Provider Dialects resolve complete database-reported type names, including vendor, array, and parameterized forms, while delegating standard parsing and registry lookup.
notes: Eight overrides, eight consumers, and extensive provider super-delegation were observed; retain its nullable result and document that this overload receives the complete reported type name before base-name lookup.

rationale: Provider Dialects resolve database-reported types using both the original and normalized base names while delegating standard registry lookup.
notes: Four overrides, five consumers, and provider super-delegation were observed; this nullable overload is independently overridden and is therefore a distinct supported variation point.

rationale: Provider Dialects replace or refine the JDBC descriptor inferred from result-set metadata while delegating standard registry resolution.
notes: Twenty-nine overrides, twenty consumers, and extensive provider super-delegation were observed; JdbcTypeRegistry is already SPI and the remaining signature types form a focused metadata-resolution boundary.

rationale: Provider Dialects normalize database-specific precision, length, scale, and display-size metadata into the length Hibernate uses for the resolved SQL type.
notes: Five overrides, two consumers, and provider super-delegation were observed; retain this focused primitive-and-String boundary and document that JDBC precision may represent character length.

rationale: Provider Dialects render inline enum declarations or named enum type references from the database type name and relational enumeration values.
notes: Eight overrides and four consumers were observed; retain the database-facing overload as the overridable hook and document that values are relational representations which might differ from Java enum constant names.

rationale: Provider enum JDBC types use this convenience to obtain a named enum type reference when only the Java enum class is available.
notes: No overrides and three provider-oriented consumers were observed; make this a non-overridable convenience delegating to the database-facing overload and limit its contract to cases where the declaration does not depend on converted relational values.

rationale: Provider Dialects render the database-specific commands which create a named enum type from its relational enumeration values.
notes: Four overrides and four consumers were observed; retain the database-facing overload as the overridable hook with an empty array meaning no separate named-type creation is required.

rationale: Named enum creation must use the relational enumeration values selected by mapping and conversion rather than independently deriving Java enum constant names.
replacement: getCreateEnumTypeCommand(String, String[]) with the mapped relational values
notes: No overrides or consumers were observed; remove this unused and potentially misleading convenience and add a versioned Migration Guide entry.

rationale: Provider Dialects render the database-specific commands which drop a named enum type.
notes: Four overrides and one direct delegating consumer were observed; retain the database-facing name overload as the overridable hook with an empty array meaning no separate named type is dropped.

rationale: Provider enum JDBC types use this convenience to derive the named enum type and obtain its database-specific drop commands.
notes: No overrides and three provider-oriented consumers were observed; make this a non-overridable convenience delegating to the String hook.

rationale: Provider Dialects render discrete-value check constraints using the mapped relational values and their JDBC type, allowing database-specific quoting and predicate syntax.
notes: One override and two consumers were observed; make this the single discrete-value variation point, migrate the Spanner family to it, and document supported character and integral JDBC types plus null-value semantics.

rationale: Provider Dialects render compact integral-range check constraints for ordinal enum mappings and may replace the inherited BETWEEN form when required.
notes: No overrides and one consumer were observed; retain the semantically distinct range hook rather than expanding ordinal ranges into potentially large discrete value collections.

rationale: The String-array overload duplicates the general discrete-value hook without carrying the JDBC type needed for complete rendering semantics.
replacement: getCheckCondition(String, Collection<?>, JdbcType) with a character JdbcType
notes: One Spanner override and two consumers were observed; migrate BooleanJavaType and the Spanner behavior to the general hook, remove the Class-overload delegation, and add a versioned Migration Guide entry.

rationale: The boxed-long overload duplicates the general discrete-value hook without carrying the JDBC type needed for complete rendering semantics.
replacement: getCheckCondition(String, Collection<?>, JdbcType) with an integral JdbcType
notes: One Spanner override and two consumers were observed; migrate BooleanJavaType and the Spanner behavior to the general hook, remove the deprecated primitive-array delegation, and add a versioned Migration Guide entry.

rationale: The enum-class convenience obscures the relational values and JDBC type which determine correct check-constraint rendering.
replacement: getCheckCondition(String, Collection<?>, JdbcType) with the mapped enum values and JdbcType
notes: No overrides and one consumer were observed; migrate EnumJavaType to the general discrete-value hook and add a versioned Migration Guide entry.

rationale: The deprecated primitive-array overload is an unused boxing bridge to another redundant overload.
replacement: getCheckCondition(String, Collection<?>, JdbcType) with an integral JdbcType
notes: Deprecated for removal since 6.5 with no overrides or consumers; remove it directly and include it in the versioned check-condition Migration Guide entry.

rationale: Provider Dialects declare whether mapped aggregate structures may be represented as database user-defined types.
notes: Four overrides and one mapping-model consumer were observed; retain this focused capability independently of the exporter selected for schema commands.

rationale: Provider Dialects supply the exporter which creates and drops their database-specific user-defined types and may select or configure a supported standard family implementation.
notes: Two overrides and two schema-management consumers were observed; Exporter is already schema SPI, while UserDefinedType and the standard UDT exporter family must form a supported provider boundary.

rationale: The UDT kind fragment is configuration of standard UDT create-command rendering rather than an independent general Dialect capability.
replacement: A supported standard UDT exporter family with configurable or overridable create-type grammar
notes: Two Oracle-family overrides and one internal exporter consumer were observed; migrate the variation into the supported family and add a versioned Migration Guide entry.

rationale: The trailing UDT clause is configuration of standard UDT create-command rendering rather than an independent general Dialect capability.
replacement: A supported standard UDT exporter family with configurable or overridable trailing create-type clauses
notes: Two DB2-family overrides and one internal exporter consumer were observed; migrate the variation into the supported family and add a versioned Migration Guide entry.

rationale: IF EXISTS placement is part of UDT drop-command grammar and should be expressed atomically by the supplied UDT exporter family instead of one of two loosely coupled Dialect booleans.
replacement: Supported UDT exporter drop-grammar configuration or strategy
notes: Five overrides and two exporter consumers were observed; migrate standard and Oracle exporter behavior and add a versioned Migration Guide entry.

rationale: IF EXISTS placement is part of UDT drop-command grammar and should be expressed atomically by the supplied UDT exporter family instead of one of two loosely coupled Dialect booleans.
replacement: Supported UDT exporter drop-grammar configuration or strategy
notes: No overrides and one internal exporter consumer were observed; remove the impossible both-true state through the replacement model and include this hook in the UDT Migration Guide entry.

rationale: Provider Dialects add database-specific JDBC metadata table-type names which Hibernate must treat as physical tables during schema extraction.
notes: Two overrides and one extraction consumer were observed; retain the focused JDK-only boundary and document the mutable list's initial contents, add-only expectation, duplicate handling, and case semantics.

rationale: Provider Dialects add database-specific JDBC metadata table-type names which Hibernate should recognize during schema extraction, including materialized views and partitioned tables.
notes: Three overrides, one extraction consumer, and provider super-delegation were observed; retain the inheritance-friendly additive hook and document the mutable list's standard and configured initial contents, add-only expectation, duplicate handling, and case semantics.

rationale: Entity-lock strategy selection should be supplied as one cohesive family instead of exposing raw engine state through a general Dialect selector and six subordinate builder callbacks.
replacement: getEntityLockingStrategyFactory() returning a supported factory driven by an EntityLockingStrategyRequest and standard profiles
notes: No overrides and two consumers were observed; move engine invocation behind the factory, define a narrow supported target/context view, retain LockingStrategy as the advanced result contract, and add a versioned Migration Guide entry.

rationale: The deprecated selector omits PessimisticLockScope and is superseded by the cohesive entity-locking factory.
replacement: getEntityLockingStrategyFactory() with the request's explicit lock scope
notes: Deprecated for removal since 7 with one community override and no consumers; migrate InterSystems IRIS to a standard or version-aware factory profile and include this overload in the versioned locking Migration Guide entry.

rationale: Per-lock-mode protected builders fragment a single strategy-selection policy and expose EntityPersister transitively through the Dialect subclass contract.
replacement: Standard entity-locking factory profiles and configurable per-mode strategy selection
notes: No overrides and one internal selector consumer were observed; provide the stock force-increment selection through the supported factory family.

rationale: Per-lock-mode protected builders fragment a single strategy-selection policy and require providers to construct concrete strategy implementations directly.
replacement: Standard entity-locking factory profiles supporting SQL-AST, select, and update pessimistic-write strategies
notes: Three community overrides and one internal selector consumer were observed; migrate Cache, RDMS, and TimesTen to the stock update profile and document the custom-factory escape hatch.

rationale: Per-lock-mode protected builders fragment a single strategy-selection policy and require providers to construct concrete strategy implementations directly.
replacement: Standard entity-locking factory profiles supporting SQL-AST, select, and update pessimistic-read strategies
notes: Three community overrides and one internal selector consumer were observed; migrate Cache, RDMS, and TimesTen to the stock update profile and document the custom-factory escape hatch.

rationale: Per-lock-mode protected builders fragment a single strategy-selection policy and expose EntityPersister transitively through the Dialect subclass contract.
replacement: Standard entity-locking factory profiles and configurable per-mode strategy selection
notes: No overrides and one internal selector consumer were observed; provide the stock optimistic force-increment selection through the supported factory family.

rationale: Per-lock-mode protected builders fragment a single strategy-selection policy and expose EntityPersister transitively through the Dialect subclass contract.
replacement: Standard entity-locking factory profiles and configurable per-mode strategy selection
notes: No overrides and one internal selector consumer were observed; provide the stock optimistic selection through the supported factory family.

rationale: Per-lock-mode protected builders fragment a single strategy-selection policy and require provider-specific routing to be spread across Dialect callbacks.
replacement: Standard entity-locking factory profiles with version-aware routing and a supported custom-factory escape hatch
notes: One HSQL legacy override and one internal selector consumer were observed; migrate its version-dependent select strategy through the family configuration and preserve deliberate custom strategy implementation support.

rationale: The size-resolution contract is a reusable type-system SPI and should not remain a nested member of the already-large Dialect class.
replacement: A top-level SizeStrategy interface in a coherent dialect type SPI package
notes: The replacement SPI package supplies implicit USE and the interface declares IMPLEMENT; preserve both resolveSize forms and ensure Size, JdbcType, and JavaType are supported signature elements.

rationale: Providers demonstrably customize the standard sizing algorithm through inheritance, but the current non-static inner implementation unnecessarily couples subclass construction to Dialect internals.
replacement: A supported StandardSizeStrategy family base bound to its Dialect or a narrow size-default context
notes: Source analysis found eight anonymous provider subclasses with extensive super.resolveSize delegation despite the generated type-level usage count; preserve this pattern through a deliberately limited supported base and migrate all built-in and community Dialects.

rationale: Provider Dialects supply the default SqlTypes code used for basic arrays and collections when no explicit mapping preference overrides it, and may delegate version-independent cases to the inherited choice.
notes: Eleven overrides, five direct consumers, and provider super-delegation were observed; document that explicit configuration wins, enumerate supported array-capable codes, and keep this distinct from per-element JdbcTypeIndicators resolution.

rationale: Provider Dialects supply the default JDBC or SqlTypes code used for Boolean mappings when no explicit mapping preference overrides it, and may delegate version-supported cases to the inherited BOOLEAN choice.
notes: Seventeen overrides, six direct consumers, and provider super-delegation were observed; document configuration precedence and the supported Boolean-compatible type codes.

rationale: Boolean type selection and registration are controlled by the preferred Boolean type code and type contributions, leaving this legacy capability disconnected from observable ORM behavior.
replacement: getPreferredSqlTypeCodeForBoolean() and contributeTypes(...)
notes: Four overrides and no consumers were observed; remove the dead hook and its overrides, and add a versioned Migration Guide entry directing providers to the effective contracts.

rationale: Provider Dialects and SQL AST translators use the database-specific lowercase function name when rendering case-folding and emulation SQL.
notes: Two overrides and ten consumers were observed, including community translators; retain the focused grammar hook and document that the result is an unquoted SQL function name rather than a complete invocation pattern.

rationale: Provider Dialects supply timestamp-add rendering patterns across temporal units, temporal representations, and native or emulated interval forms, and may delegate supported combinations to a family implementation.
notes: Forty-three overrides, two direct consumers, and provider super-delegation were observed; retain the primary grammar hook, document all three placeholder positions and unsupported-combination behavior, and include IntervalType in the supported provider boundary.

rationale: Provider Dialects supply timestamp-difference rendering patterns across temporal units and operand representations and may delegate supported combinations to a family implementation.
notes: Forty-two overrides, five direct consumers, and provider super-delegation were observed; retain the primary grammar hook and document all three placeholder positions, argument order, result-unit semantics, and unsupported-combination behavior.

rationale: No Hibernate behavior consults this legacy capability; current-timestamp expression and selection behavior are determined by the active rendering and current-timestamp hooks.
replacement: Current timestamp rendering plus getCurrentTimestampSelectString() and isCurrentTimestampSelectStringCallable() where selection is required
notes: Three overrides and no consumers were observed; remove the disconnected method and overrides, and add a versioned Migration Guide entry identifying the effective replacement contracts.

rationale: Provider Dialects supply their database's functional-dependency analysis profile so Hibernate can safely reduce GROUP BY and ORDER BY expressions.
notes: Sixteen overrides and one consumer were observed; retain the focused getter but replace the interface and mutable-looking implementation pair with a supported immutable profile value and named stock profiles in a coherent SPI package.

rationale: Provider Dialects declare support independently for each SQL FETCH clause form, and provider translators consult the capability when selecting native rendering or emulation.
notes: Thirteen overrides and fourteen consumers were observed, including provider translators; retain the focused capability and include FetchClauseType in the supported provider boundary with exhaustive per-value compatibility tests.

rationale: Provider Dialects declare native window-function support used by query translation, pagination emulation, temporary-table population, and provider translators.
notes: Thirty-two overrides and fourteen consumers were observed; retain the widely used capability and document that it denotes the baseline window-function feature rather than every optional window clause.

rationale: Provider Dialects separately declare support for ROWS, RANGE, and GROUPS frame clauses when baseline window functions exist.
notes: One CUBRID override but no consumers were observed; retain the semantically distinct capability only by wiring it into SQL AST validation or rendering and adding a compatibility test so the SPI promise has observable effect.

rationale: Provider Dialects render the database-specific ALTER TABLE fragment for changing a column type, or return null when the operation is unsupported.
notes: Sixteen overrides and one schema-migration consumer were observed; make the nullable result the sole capability signal and document the distinct quoted column name, rendered type, and full column-definition inputs.

rationale: A separate Boolean duplicates the nullable alter-column fragment and permits contradictory states between capability and rendering.
replacement: A non-null result from getAlterColumnTypeString(String, String, String)
notes: Sixteen overrides paired with the rendering overrides and one consumer were observed; update StandardTableMigrator to call the renderer when a type change is needed, apply only non-null fragments, migrate provider pairs, and add a versioned Migration Guide entry.

rationale: Provider Dialects render database-specific trailing CREATE TABLE options such as storage-engine or row-locking clauses and may compose or delegate family defaults.
notes: Four overrides, three consumers, and provider super-delegation were observed; retain the focused String hook and document whether leading whitespace belongs to the returned fragment plus its application to persistent temporary tables.

rationale: Although previously approved as a focused hook, type presence is one of the coupled ordering rules for generated-column definitions and belongs with the column-definition grammar now being consolidated.
replacement: ColumnDefinitionSupport generated-column type-presence policy
notes: Three overrides and one schema-rendering consumer were observed; this explicitly supersedes the earlier retention decision, preserves typed and type-inferred grammars, and tests the policy together with generated-clause and nullability ordering.

rationale: Although previously approved as a focused primitive hook, the locator type is valid only together with the row-id expression and optional physical declaration now being consolidated.
replacement: RowIdSupport locator JDBC or extended SqlTypes code
notes: Nine overrides and two consumers were observed; this supersedes the earlier retention decision, preserves provider-translator access through the supported profile, and validates type availability with the locator expression.

rationale: This Boolean is one branch of a prioritized null-binding policy and can conflict with the independent setObject(null) capability.
replacement: getObjectNullBindingStrategy() returning a supported null-binding profile
notes: Four overrides and two consumers were observed; migrate PostgreSQL, H2, MySQL, and GaussDB to the SET_NULL_WITH_NULL_TYPE profile and add a versioned Migration Guide entry.

rationale: This Boolean is one branch of a prioritized null-binding policy and its true value silently takes precedence over the setNull capability.
replacement: getObjectNullBindingStrategy() returning a supported null-binding profile
notes: One SQL Server override and two consumers were observed; replace the Boolean pair with explicit SET_OBJECT, SET_NULL_WITH_NULL_TYPE, and metadata-derived SET_NULL profiles in a coherent SPI package, update ObjectNullResolvingJdbcType, and add compatibility tests and a versioned Migration Guide entry.

rationale: This is a fixed set of legacy mapping-level quote markers, not database behavior supplied or consumed by a Dialect provider.
replacement: Identifier quote-marker recognition or a private internal quote-pair helper
notes: The generated inventory misses the two static field reads in Column and Alias; migrate those internal consumers, remove the public constant from Dialect, and add a versioned Migration Guide entry.

rationale: This is the closing half of the fixed legacy mapping-level quote-marker table, not a provider extension contract.
replacement: Identifier quote-marker recognition or a private internal quote-pair helper
notes: The generated inventory misses the two static field reads in Column and Alias; preserve the backtick, double-quote, and bracket pairings internally, remove the public constant from Dialect, and add a versioned Migration Guide entry.

rationale: Provider Dialects supply their database's identifier opening delimiter, while provider support code may consume it when parsing or rendering identifiers.
notes: Seven overrides and five generated call sites were observed; retain the primitive hook and test both symmetric and asymmetric quote pairs.

rationale: Provider Dialects supply their database's identifier closing delimiter, while provider support code may consume it when parsing or rendering identifiers.
notes: Seven overrides and five generated call sites were observed; retain the primitive hook and test both symmetric and asymmetric quote pairs.

rationale: Provider Dialects may customize complete identifier rendering for database-specific exceptions and may delegate ordinary identifiers to the inherited delimiter-based implementation.
notes: Two Sybase overrides and three call sites were observed; retain the nullable focused rendering hook and cover the Sybase temporary-table exception as well as normal delegation.

rationale: Provider-side delegates and rendering helpers need the convenience which converts Hibernate's backtick marker to the active database delimiters, but database variation belongs in the delimiter and complete-rendering hooks.
notes: No overrides and nine call sites were observed, including a community UniqueDelegate; retain it as a provider convenience but make it non-overridable, precisely document its marker-conversion semantics, and add a Migration Guide note for any unsupported override.

rationale: Provider Dialects customize whether and how a collation name is quoted in a column definition independently of general identifier quoting.
notes: Three overrides and one schema-rendering consumer were observed; retain the focused rendering hook and test both the inherited pass-through and quoted database forms.

rationale: Provider Dialects render binary literals using database-specific introducers, encodings, and casts, and provider translators or JDBC literal formatters may invoke the renderer.
notes: Twelve overrides and one generated consumer were observed; retain the focused appender hook and cover representative hexadecimal, function, and cast forms without exposing an intermediate String contract.

rationale: Provider Dialects render database-specific Boolean literal expressions and provider translators may append them directly without allocating an intermediate String.
notes: Twenty-one overrides and five consumers were observed, including provider super-delegation; retain this as the sole Boolean-literal implementation hook and test native Boolean and numeric emulation forms.

rationale: Provider Dialects and provider JDBC types may render duration literals using database-specific interval syntax while delegating supported forms to the inherited SQL-oriented implementation.
notes: No overrides and three consumers were observed; retain the focused duration hook because interval syntax is database behavior, and add coverage for whole-unit and fractional-second forms, including the inherited renderer's duplicated interval introducer path.

rationale: Provider translators render general temporal amounts through a database-specific interval hook which dispatches durations and calendar periods.
notes: No overrides and one SQL AST translator consumer were observed; retain the general hook so providers can customize period or combined-unit syntax, and test Duration delegation, Period rendering, and unsupported TemporalAmount behavior.

rationale: Provider Dialects render string literals with database-specific escaping rules, and provider functions and translators may invoke the same renderer.
notes: Four overrides and nine consumers were observed, including community JSON renderers; retain the focused appender hook and test standard escaping plus MySQL-style escape behavior.

rationale: Provider Dialects render UUID literals using database-specific casts, functions, or native syntax, and provider JDBC literal formatters may invoke the renderer.
notes: Three overrides and one generated consumer were observed; retain the focused appender hook and cover native UUID, binary-oriented, and cast-based forms.

rationale: Provider translators and legacy SQL rendering helpers sometimes require the complete Boolean literal as a String, but all database variation is already expressed by appendBooleanValueString(...).
notes: No overrides and two consumers were observed; retain it as a non-overridable convenience delegating to the supported appender hook, and add a Migration Guide note for any unsupported override.

rationale: Provider Dialects render the current or local date expression used to register the HQL and JPQL temporal functions and may reuse it in provider SQL rendering.
notes: Eleven overrides and one registry consumer were observed; retain the focused expression hook and document that the result is a complete unparenthesized SQL expression.

rationale: Provider Dialects render the legacy JDBC current-time expression whose no-time-zone semantics may differ from the ANSI current_time expression.
notes: Twenty-two overrides and three consumers were observed, including provider delegation; retain the focused hook and test its deliberate semantic relationship to currentLocalTime().

rationale: Provider Dialects render the legacy JDBC current-timestamp expression whose no-time-zone semantics may differ from ANSI current_timestamp and which is reused by generated-value and temporal mapping support.
notes: Twenty-six overrides and twenty-one consumers were observed, including provider delegation; retain the focused hook and document expression type and stability separately.

rationale: Provider Dialects render the no-time-zone local-time expression and may delegate to currentTime() where the database uses the same expression.
notes: Four overrides and one registry consumer were observed; retain the focused semantic hook and test both inherited delegation and distinct local-time syntax.

rationale: Provider Dialects render the no-time-zone local-timestamp expression and may delegate to currentTimestamp() where the database uses the same expression.
notes: Four overrides and four consumers were observed, including provider delegation; retain the focused semantic hook and test both inherited delegation and distinct local-timestamp syntax.

rationale: Provider Dialects render the current timestamp-with-time-zone expression used for OffsetDateTime semantics and may share it with another current temporal expression where database typing permits.
notes: Thirteen overrides and seven consumers were observed, including provider delegation; retain the focused semantic hook and document that the result type, not merely its spelling, distinguishes it from currentTimestamp().

rationale: This unconsumed Boolean duplicates the availability of current-timestamp retrieval and permits contradictory combinations with the command and callable hooks.
replacement: A nullable getCurrentTimestampSelection() profile containing the command and JDBC callable flag
notes: Twenty-nine overrides and no consumers were observed; migrate each three-method provider set to one optional immutable profile and add a versioned Migration Guide entry.

rationale: The retrieval command and its JDBC preparation mode are one atomic provider-supplied selection strategy and should not be independently overridable.
replacement: A nullable getCurrentTimestampSelection() profile containing the command and JDBC callable flag
notes: Thirty overrides and one consumer were observed; migrate CurrentTimestampGeneration to obtain and validate one selection profile, and cover absent, prepared-statement, and callable forms.

rationale: This Boolean is meaningful only together with the current-timestamp selection command and can currently contradict its availability.
replacement: A nullable getCurrentTimestampSelection() profile containing the command and JDBC callable flag
notes: Twenty-nine overrides and one consumer were observed; migrate paired overrides into the immutable selection profile and add compatibility tests and a versioned Migration Guide entry.

rationale: Provider Dialects declare whether the current-timestamp expression is transaction-stable, which controls temporal changeset identity independently of how a timestamp is selected through JDBC.
notes: Six overrides and two consumers were observed; retain the distinct capability and test stable and volatile database semantics separately from the selection profile.

rationale: Provider Dialects supply vendor-specific SQLException conversion in addition to Hibernate's standard JDBC hierarchy and SQL-state delegates, and family implementations may delegate an unsupported version to the inherited null result.
notes: Thirty-three overrides and two consumers were observed; retain the nullable focused factory and explicitly classify SQLExceptionConversionDelegate for provider implementation as well as use.

rationale: Provider Dialects supply vendor-message constraint-name extraction used both by their own conversion delegates and by Hibernate's standard conversion chain.
notes: Thirty overrides and twenty-six consumers were observed, mostly provider delegates; retain the focused getter and explicitly classify ViolatedConstraintNameExtractor for provider implementation as well as use.

rationale: Provider Dialects determine whether a particular failed statement causes the database transaction itself to enter rollback-only state, independently of how the exception is converted.
notes: Two overrides and two consumers were observed; retain the SQLException parameter to preserve conditional provider policies even though the current PostgreSQL-family overrides return true for every exception, and test both transaction-state outcomes.

rationale: Provider Dialects configure or supply identifier normalization using driver metadata, registered keywords, database casing, and qualification rules, and family implementations commonly delegate to the inherited builder path.
notes: Twenty-nine overrides and thirty-two consumers were observed, predominantly provider super-delegation; retain the nullable focused builder hook and ensure IdentifierHelper and IdentifierHelperBuilder have the roles required by provider implementations.

rationale: Provider Dialects supply the separator used between catalog and following name parts when JDBC metadata is unavailable or insufficient.
notes: One Informix override and one environment consumer were observed; retain the focused scalar capability and test the standard dot and Informix colon forms.

rationale: Provider identifier helpers and SQL renderers may inspect the completed normalized keyword set, but mutation must occur only through the supported registration lifecycle.
notes: No overrides and three consumers were observed, including a community identifier helper; retain it as a non-overridable read-only view and return an immutable Set so callers cannot mutate Dialect construction state.

rationale: Provider Dialects supply the safe length Hibernate may use for generated SQL aliases after reserving suffix space, and provider rendering helpers may use the same limit.
notes: Twelve overrides and one consumer were observed; retain the focused limit, distinguish it from the database identifier limit, and test generated alias truncation and suffix preservation.

rationale: Provider Dialects supply the database's general identifier-length limit, while provider type and temporary-object support may use it when constructing auxiliary names.
notes: Twenty-five overrides and three consumers were observed, including a Dialect-specific JDBC type; retain the focused limit and test temporary-table, CTE, and auxiliary-type name truncation.

rationale: ANSI keyword initialization is invariant Hibernate construction work, while overriding a method from the superclass constructor creates a fragile provider lifecycle solely to append vendor words.
replacement: Internal non-overridable ANSI initialization plus protected registerKeyword(String) and registerKeywords(String...) provider helpers
notes: Eighteen overrides and twenty consumers were observed; migrate vendor additions to provider construction, remove the overridable constructor hook, preserve superclass-before-provider ordering, and add a versioned Migration Guide entry.

rationale: Provider Dialects register normalized vendor keywords during construction and may filter inaccurate driver-reported words before they enter the completed set.
notes: One MariaDB filtering override and twenty generated consumers were observed despite many source-level calls; retain the protected hook, document construction-only use and lowercase normalization, and add a protected bulk registration convenience.

rationale: Provider constructors which delegate through a DatabaseVersion-based family constructor need a supported convenience for importing driver-reported keywords from DialectResolutionInfo.
notes: No overrides and twenty-nine provider constructor consumers were observed; retain it as a non-overridable protected convenience which dispatches each word through registerKeyword(String), and document null or empty metadata behavior.

rationale: This broad execution-level orchestration hook exposes QueryOptions and is overridden only to reverse the relative order of a query hint and user comment.
replacement: Internal query-decoration orchestration plus a focused getQueryHintPlacement() SPI capability
notes: Three PostgreSQL-family overrides and two execution consumers were observed; introduce a supported placement enum for hint-before-comment versus hint-after-comment, migrate the duplicated overrides, keep QueryOptions internal to orchestration, and add a versioned Migration Guide entry.

rationale: Provider Dialects render and position an ordered set of structured database hints against the complete finalized SQL statement, preserving per-hint boundaries where database syntax requires them.
notes: Five overrides and four consumers were observed; retain this as the primary query-hint rendering hook, document immutable ordered input and unchanged-SQL fallback, and test list-sensitive Cockroach, HANA, and Oracle forms.

rationale: Provider Dialects render a database-specific combined hint string and list-based implementations may delegate to it after applying their database's separator convention.
notes: Twelve overrides and five consumers were observed, including provider super-delegation; retain the focused compatibility hook and test prefix, statement-keyword, suffix, and USE INDEX placements.

rationale: USE INDEX insertion is a reusable provider composition helper for a query-hint family, not state or behavior belonging to every Dialect instance.
replacement: A supported query-hint SPI utility or strategy for USE INDEX insertion
notes: Five provider consumers and no overrides were observed; move the helper from Dialect into a coherent query-hint SPI package, retain USE classification there, test recognized and unchanged query shapes, and add a versioned Migration Guide entry.

rationale: Escaping nested SQL comment delimiters is generic SQL rendering support used by translators and legacy statement builders, not database-specific Dialect behavior.
replacement: A supported SQL comment escaping utility in the engine-level SQL rendering SPI
notes: Seven consumers and no overrides were observed, including a provider translator; move the static helper to a coherent SQL rendering SPI package, preserve provider USE, and migrate all callers with a versioned Migration Guide entry.

rationale: This unoverridden protected helper exists only to support the broad addSqlHintOrComment() override pattern eliminated by focused placement metadata.
replacement: Internal query-decoration orchestration using the supported SQL comment escaper
notes: No overrides and four orchestration consumers were observed; internalize comment insertion after migrating PostgreSQL-family ordering, and add a Migration Guide entry directing providers to the focused placement and escaping contracts.

rationale: No maintained Dialect customizes this legacy post-render transformation hook and its sole consumer is the legacy SimpleSelect builder.
replacement: No replacement; use the SQL AST translator or a focused query-hint renderer for supported provider variation
notes: No overrides and one consumer were observed; remove the hook and direct any external database rendering variation to the supported translator or hint contracts in the versioned Migration Guide.

rationale: This superclass-constructor callback exposes mutable Dialect state and combines invariant Hibernate defaults, typed provider defaults, and arbitrary configuration contributions in one fragile lifecycle hook.
replacement: A protected contributeDefaultProperties(Properties) SPI hook invoked once after Dialect construction against an isolated property bag
notes: Five overrides and six consumers were observed; migrate all arbitrary defaults to the contribution hook, remove the overridable constructor callback, define one-time invocation and precedence, and add a versioned Migration Guide entry.

rationale: This is an engine bootstrap snapshot accessor rather than a contract providers or application code need to call; providers should contribute defaults through the focused lifecycle hook instead of mutating returned Dialect state.
notes: No overrides and nine consumers were observed, including five uses from current initialization overrides; retain the engine accessor as internal, return a defensive or immutable completed snapshot, and remove provider mutation through this method.

rationale: This typed method is immediately converted to the STATEMENT_BATCH_SIZE property and has no independent runtime consumer or semantics.
replacement: contributeDefaultProperties(Properties) setting STATEMENT_BATCH_SIZE
notes: Twenty-two overrides and one initialization consumer were observed; migrate values to the unified contribution hook, preserve application-setting precedence over Dialect defaults, and add a versioned Migration Guide entry.

rationale: This typed method is immediately converted to the NON_CONTEXTUAL_LOB_CREATION property and has no independent runtime consumer.
replacement: contributeDefaultProperties(Properties) setting NON_CONTEXTUAL_LOB_CREATION
notes: Seven overrides and one initialization consumer were observed; migrate values to the unified contribution hook and preserve explicit application override precedence.

rationale: This typed method is immediately converted to the USE_GET_GENERATED_KEYS property and has no independent runtime consumer.
replacement: contributeDefaultProperties(Properties) setting USE_GET_GENERATED_KEYS
notes: Six overrides and one initialization consumer were observed; migrate values to the unified contribution hook and preserve explicit application override precedence.

rationale: Provider Dialects supply the safest default JDBC result-set scrolling mode for their driver and family implementations may delegate the standard choice.
notes: Six overrides and two consumers were observed, including provider super-delegation; retain the directly consumed typed capability and cover insensitive, sensitive, and forward-only defaults.

rationale: Provider Dialects declare whether JDBC warnings should be logged by default when driver behavior makes warning retrieval useful or excessively noisy.
notes: Three MySQL-family overrides and one environment consumer were observed; retain the directly consumed capability and preserve explicit configuration precedence in tests.

rationale: Default exact-numeric precision is one immutable dimension of the database's type-sizing limits and should be supplied coherently with the related precision, length, and capacity values.
replacement: getTypeSizingProfile() returning a supported immutable TypeSizingProfile
notes: Fourteen overrides and eight consumers were observed, including provider translators; migrate the scalar into the profile, preserve provider read access, and add a versioned Migration Guide entry.

rationale: Default timestamp fractional precision is one immutable dimension of the database's type-sizing limits and is distinct from the native unit used for temporal arithmetic.
replacement: getTypeSizingProfile() returning a supported immutable TypeSizingProfile
notes: Eleven overrides and twelve consumers were observed; migrate the scalar into the profile, document digits-of-fraction semantics, and retain provider read access through the profile.

rationale: Default interval-second scale is one immutable dimension of the database's type-sizing limits and should be composed with the other default precisions.
replacement: getTypeSizingProfile() returning a supported immutable TypeSizingProfile
notes: Five overrides and one consumer were observed; migrate the scalar into the profile and document its relationship to Duration nanosecond resolution.

rationale: Default generated LOB length is one immutable dimension of the database's type-sizing limits and is consumed by sizing strategies rather than representing a separate behavior family.
replacement: getTypeSizingProfile() returning a supported immutable TypeSizingProfile
notes: Six overrides and eight consumers were observed, mostly provider SizeStrategy implementations; migrate the value into the profile and preserve provider USE from supported sizing strategies.

rationale: The database precision representing Java float is one immutable type-sizing dimension and should be supplied with double and exact-numeric precision.
replacement: getTypeSizingProfile() returning a supported immutable TypeSizingProfile
notes: Ten overrides and four consumers were observed; migrate the scalar into the profile and document whether the database interprets it in binary or decimal digits.

rationale: The database precision representing Java double is one immutable type-sizing dimension and should be supplied with float and exact-numeric precision.
replacement: getTypeSizingProfile() returning a supported immutable TypeSizingProfile
notes: Five overrides and two consumers were observed; migrate the scalar into the profile and document whether the database interprets it in binary or decimal digits.

rationale: The maximum parameter accepted by a VARCHAR-like type is one member of a coherent character and binary length/capacity profile.
replacement: getTypeSizingProfile() returning a supported immutable TypeSizingProfile
notes: Thirty-two overrides and nineteen consumers were observed, including provider type registration; migrate the scalar into the profile, preserve provider USE, and distinguish parameter limit from physical capacity.

rationale: The maximum parameter accepted by an NVARCHAR-like type is one member of a coherent character and binary length/capacity profile.
replacement: getTypeSizingProfile() returning a supported immutable TypeSizingProfile
notes: Six overrides and thirteen consumers were observed; migrate the scalar into the profile, preserve inheritance from the VARCHAR value as a stock default, and document character rather than byte units.

rationale: The maximum parameter accepted by a VARBINARY-like type is one member of a coherent character and binary length/capacity profile.
replacement: getTypeSizingProfile() returning a supported immutable TypeSizingProfile
notes: Twenty-two overrides and fourteen consumers were observed, including provider type registration; migrate the scalar into the profile and document byte-length units.

rationale: The physical capacity of a VARCHAR-like column is related to but may exceed its maximum parameterized type length, making it a validated member of the sizing profile.
replacement: getTypeSizingProfile() returning a supported immutable TypeSizingProfile
notes: Five overrides and two consumers were observed; migrate the scalar into the profile and validate capacity is not less than the corresponding parameter limit.

rationale: The physical capacity of an NVARCHAR-like column is a derived-by-default but independently representable member of the sizing profile.
replacement: getTypeSizingProfile() returning a supported immutable TypeSizingProfile
notes: No overrides and two consumers were observed; migrate the scalar into the profile, default it from max NVARCHAR length, and make profile customization available without retaining another Dialect hook.

rationale: The physical capacity of a VARBINARY-like column is a derived-by-default but independently representable member of the sizing profile.
replacement: getTypeSizingProfile() returning a supported immutable TypeSizingProfile
notes: No overrides and one consumer were observed; migrate the scalar into the profile, default it from max VARBINARY length, and make profile customization available without retaining another Dialect hook.

rationale: Provider Dialects supply and provider translators consume the native temporal-arithmetic unit expressed as a number of nanoseconds, which is semantic behavior rather than a column-sizing default.
notes: Twenty-five overrides and one generated consumer were observed; retain the focused capability, require a positive power-of-ten-compatible unit where applicable, and test consistency with timestamp arithmetic patterns.

rationale: Provider Dialects decide whether mappings exceeding inline character or binary capacity should switch to materialized LOB JDBC types, independently of the numeric capacity limits themselves.
notes: Six overrides and three consumers were observed; retain the focused policy capability, document its default relationship to supportsMaterializedLobAccess(), and test both promotion and no-promotion behavior.

rationale: No Hibernate behavior consults this historical, vaguely defined driver capability, and its semantics overlap several now-focused LOB creation, binding, and materialization contracts.
replacement: The focused LOB creation, binding, materialized-access, and value-access contracts
notes: Five overrides and no consumers were observed; remove the dead hook and its overrides, and add a versioned Migration Guide entry naming the effective replacement contracts.

rationale: Hibernate no longer branches on in-place locator mutation propagation and the method's own documentation identifies JDBC metadata rather than Dialect as the likely authority.
replacement: No Dialect replacement; use JDBC locator update/copy behavior where a future consumer requires it
notes: Twenty-five overrides and no consumers were observed; remove the disconnected hook and add a versioned Migration Guide entry explaining that replacing a LOB value remains the supported persistence path.

rationale: No Hibernate behavior consults this historical locator-lifetime capability, and actual materialization is controlled by active LOB creator and JDBC access paths.
replacement: The active LOB creation and materialized-access contracts
notes: Eleven overrides and no consumers were observed; remove the dead hook and its overrides, and add a versioned Migration Guide entry.

rationale: Provider Dialects evaluate database and driver metadata to determine whether JDBC Connection LOB factories are usable for contextual creation.
notes: Six overrides and one consumer were observed; retain the metadata-dependent focused capability, document nullable metadata expectations, and test supported and rejected driver-version paths.

rationale: Provider Dialects select stream versus materialized LOB binding according to driver semantics and runtime Dialect state, and provider JDBC support may consume the same choice.
notes: Ten overrides and three consumers were observed; retain the focused binding capability and test stream, materialized, and Oracle application-continuity behavior.

rationale: Provider Dialects independently declare whether contextual LOB creators must use JDBC Connection factory methods instead of Hibernate locator implementations.
notes: Nine overrides and two consumers were observed; retain this independently configurable creation capability despite its inherited default being derived from stream binding, and test all meaningful combinations.

rationale: Provider Dialects declare whether their drivers support materialized byte and string APIs for LOB values, controlling type registration and capacity-driven promotion policy.
notes: Three PostgreSQL-family overrides and two consumers were observed; retain the focused access capability and test materialized JDBC descriptor registration and its policy interaction.

rationale: Provider Dialects declare whether LOB assignments must be ordered after all other values in insert and update statements.
notes: Two Oracle overrides and two mutation-builder consumers were observed; retain the focused DML-ordering capability and test insert and update assignment order.

rationale: Provider Dialects classify JDBC and extended SqlTypes codes as locator-oriented LOBs while registering database-specific DDL and JDBC types, and may delegate standard codes to the inherited classification.
notes: Three PostgreSQL-family overrides and nine consumers were observed, including provider type registration and super-delegation; retain the protected type-classification hook and document the supported type-code domain.

rationale: A separate Boolean duplicates whether the database supplies a VALUE LOB DDL fragment and permits contradictory support and rendering results.
replacement: A non-null result from getValueLOBFragmentForExtraCreateTableInfo(String)
notes: One Oracle override and three consumers were observed; make the nullable fragment the sole support signal, migrate the consumers, and add a versioned Migration Guide entry.

rationale: Provider Dialects render the column-specific extra CREATE TABLE fragment for VALUE LOB access or return null when the feature is unsupported.
notes: One Oracle override and three JDBC type consumers were observed; retain the focused renderer, replace the inherited empty String with a nullable unsupported result, and test both absent and Oracle VALUE LOB forms.

rationale: This deprecated Boolean bridge duplicates pessimistic-lock style metadata and has no remaining overrides or consumers.
replacement: getLockingSupport().getMetadata().getPessimisticLockStyle()
notes: Remove the bridge after migrating any compatibility tests, and add a versioned Migration Guide entry directing providers to LockingSupport.Metadata.

rationale: This deprecated Boolean bridge duplicates timeout-specific locking metadata and cannot express whether SKIP LOCKED is implemented in the query or through another mechanism.
replacement: getLockingSupport().getMetadata().getLockTimeoutType(Timeouts.SKIP_LOCKED)
notes: One community override and legacy rendering consumers were observed; migrate them with the locking-rendering family and add a versioned Migration Guide entry.

rationale: This deprecated Boolean bridge duplicates timeout-specific locking metadata and cannot express whether NO WAIT is implemented in the query or through another mechanism.
replacement: getLockingSupport().getMetadata().getLockTimeoutType(Timeouts.NO_WAIT)
notes: One community override and legacy rendering consumers were observed; migrate them with the locking-rendering family and add a versioned Migration Guide entry.

rationale: This deprecated Boolean bridge duplicates timeout-specific locking metadata and collapses finite wait support into an imprecise yes-or-no answer.
replacement: getLockingSupport().getMetadata().getLockTimeoutType(Timeout)
notes: One community override and legacy rendering consumers were observed; migrate them with the locking-rendering family and add a versioned Migration Guide entry.
