rationale: This deprecated Dialect-level getter is a pass-through to the supported locking metadata contract.

rationale: Scalar DISTINCT FROM is a core predicate-syntax capability used by translator rendering and as a prerequisite for row-value DISTINCT FROM support.
replacement: PredicateSupport scalar DISTINCT_FROM capability
notes: Twenty-one overrides and six production consumers were observed, including provider translators; preserve provider USE and make RowValueSupport consistency depend on this profile capability.

rationale: IS TRUE and IS FALSE form a focused truthness-predicate syntax capability used to select native rendering or Boolean comparison emulation.
replacement: PredicateSupport TRUTHNESS capability
notes: Eight overrides and one translator consumer were observed; preserve provider configuration and test true, false, and negated forms through native and emulated rendering.

rationale: Whether a predicate may occur in a value-expression context is a predicate placement rule used when choosing aggregate Boolean emulation.
replacement: PredicateSupport EXPRESSION_PLACEMENT capability
notes: Three community overrides and one function-registration consumer were observed; preserve provider configuration, expose the profile as USE SPI, and test every/any emulation selection.

rationale: Aggregate FILTER-clause support is a function-expression grammar capability used to select native rendering or CASE-based emulation.
replacement: An immutable supported FunctionSyntaxSupport profile with an AGGREGATE_FILTER capability
notes: Nine overrides and two runtime consumers were observed; preserve provider configuration, expose provider USE through the profile, and test native and emulated filtered aggregates.

rationale: Window-function PARTITION BY support is stable function-expression grammar information used by feature checks and required by the Dialect compatibility test kit.
replacement: FunctionSyntaxSupport WINDOW_PARTITION capability
notes: Twenty-four overrides were observed; the generated production inventory omits consumers in hibernate-testing, so migrate DialectChecks and DialectFeatureChecks and preserve this capability for provider compatibility testing.

rationale: A database's default null ordering is consumed together with its support for explicit NULLS FIRST and NULLS LAST syntax when selecting native rendering or emulation.
replacement: An immutable supported NullOrderingSupport profile containing the default NullOrdering and explicit-precedence capability
notes: Eighteen overrides and four consumers were observed; preserve provider USE through the profile, classify NullOrdering as supported USE SPI, and test ascending and descending defaults for every ordering value.

rationale: Explicit null-precedence syntax cannot be interpreted correctly without the database's default null ordering and belongs in the same focused profile.
replacement: NullOrderingSupport explicit NULLS_FIRST_LAST capability
notes: Seventeen overrides and four production consumers plus a testing feature check were observed; migrate provider translators and tests and cover native and CASE-based emulation.

rationale: Provider Dialects must be able to state whether query clauses may reference select items by one-based ordinal, which controls expression rendering in the SQL AST translator.
notes: No in-repository override and one translator consumer were observed; retain this focused scalar hook rather than broadening NullOrderingSupport, and cover unsupported fallback rendering in the compatibility test kit.

rationale: The Oracle-specific name exposes one rendering of the broader single-row-table facility used by query and mutation translation.
replacement: An immutable supported SingleRowTableSupport profile containing the reusable single-row table expression
notes: Twenty-nine overrides and twenty-five consumers were observed, including provider Dialects and translator paths; preserve provider USE through the profile, use semantic naming, and add a versioned Migration Guide entry.

rationale: The optional FROM fragment for otherwise table-less SELECT statements is the context-specific rendering paired with the reusable single-row table expression.
replacement: SingleRowTableSupport optional select-only FROM fragment
notes: Twenty-four overrides and four generated consumers were observed, with additional translator-internal calls through its protected delegate; permit an empty fragment, preserve version-dependent variants, and test fragment-only, table-expression, alias, and restricting-WHERE forms.

rationale: Provider Dialects must be able to select ANSI CROSS JOIN rendering or comma-join emulation independently of single-row-table support.
notes: Five overrides and one base-translator consumer were observed; retain the focused scalar capability and test both native CROSS JOIN and emulated comma-join rendering.

rationale: Provider Dialects implement database-specific datetime-format conversion consumed by function rendering and SQL AST translation.
notes: Thirty-five overrides and two generated consumers were observed; retain the focused rendering hook, keep SqlAppender supported USE SPI, and cover provider formatting plus unsupported-format behavior in the compatibility test kit.

rationale: Provider Dialects implement the database's extraction pattern and commonly delegate unchanged temporal units to the inherited standard pattern.
notes: Thirty-two overrides and twenty-two consumers were observed, including provider super-delegation and custom function descriptors; classify TemporalUnit for provider USE and test every supported and rejected field category.

rationale: Provider Dialects translate semantic temporal fields to database tokens and commonly delegate standard fields to the inherited implementation.
notes: Twenty-three overrides and twenty-one consumers were observed; retain the focused helper, preserve super-delegation, and keep its TemporalUnit boundary supported.

rationale: Provider Dialects translate semantic duration units used by timestamp arithmetic and may delegate standard units to the inherited implementation.
notes: Five overrides and eleven consumers were observed, including provider arithmetic-pattern methods; retain the focused helper and test legal duration units and rejected field-only units.

rationale: Provider Dialects supply whether temporal precision adjustment rounds or truncates, which directly affects bound and generated temporal values.
notes: Eleven overrides and one DateTimeUtils consumer were observed; retain the scalar semantic hook and test boundary values at each supported temporal precision.

rationale: Provider Dialects supply and consume whether UTC offsets may be rendered directly in time and timestamp literals.
notes: Twelve overrides and twenty-four provider-side consumers were observed; retain the focused capability, preserve provider USE, and test offset-preserving and JDBC-time-zone-normalizing literal rendering.

rationale: No Hibernate translation, execution, or compatibility-test path consults this historical declaration, so its overrides do not affect behavior.
replacement: No replacement; express any required arithmetic variation in timestampaddPattern(), timestampdiffPattern(), or the SQL AST translator
notes: Four HANA and Sybase family overrides and no consumers were observed; remove the dead hook and overrides and document the effective rendering extension points in the Migration Guide.

rationale: Provider Dialects supply whether Hibernate may create and drop catalog namespaces during schema management.
notes: Three MySQL-family and SingleStore overrides and three schema-management consumers were observed, with additional testing checks; retain the compact Boolean boundary and test namespace-management gating.

rationale: Provider Dialects supply the database-specific SQL commands Hibernate executes to create a catalog namespace.
notes: Three overrides and two schema-management consumers were observed; retain the String input and String-array result consistently with schema namespace creation and test multiple-command ordering.

rationale: Provider Dialects supply the database-specific SQL commands Hibernate executes to drop a catalog namespace.
notes: Three overrides and one schema-management consumer were observed; retain the compact boundary consistently with schema namespace removal and test multiple-command ordering and disabled catalog management.

rationale: Provider Dialects supply table creation and removal behavior and may reuse or decorate Hibernate's standard table exporter.
notes: Fourteen overrides and four consumers were observed, including provider access to an inherited exporter; keep Exporter and its model boundary supported and provide supported standard family bases or composition points without exposing built-in leaves wholesale.

rationale: Provider Dialects may supply database-specific table-alter planning when standard column migration is insufficient.
notes: No in-repository override and one schema-migration consumer were observed; retain the deliberately typed schema SPI hook, audit all TableMigrator signature types, and provide a supported standard implementation or composable base.

rationale: Provider Dialects may supply coordinated table truncation and constraint-disable or re-enable behavior for database-specific cleaning requirements.
notes: No in-repository override and three truncation consumers were observed; retain the Incubating Cleaner strategy, audit its model signatures, and provide supported construction or a standard composable implementation.

rationale: Provider Dialects supply nonstandard index creation and removal behavior through the schema Exporter contract.
notes: Two community overrides and two schema-management consumers were observed; retain the strategy supplier and provide a supported standard base or composition point for minor syntax variation.

rationale: Provider Dialects supply foreign-key DDL behavior and may delegate supported database versions to Hibernate's inherited standard exporter.
notes: Two community overrides and six consumers were observed, including provider super-delegation; retain the strategy and provide a supported standard family base or composable renderer.

rationale: Provider Dialects may supply runtime temporary-table create, drop, and truncate rendering independently of the selected temporary-table lifecycle strategy.
notes: No in-repository override and three runtime consumers were observed; retain the explicit strategy boundary, move it to a temporary-table SPI package, audit TemporaryTable and session signature types, and provide supported standard composition.

rationale: Provider Dialects supply the coherent column-level, table-level, and alter-table strategy for unique constraints.
notes: Twenty-one overrides and four consumers were observed; move UniqueDelegate to unique.spi and expose supported standard factories, bases, or composition while keeping concrete built-in leaves internal where appropriate.

rationale: AuxiliaryDatabaseObject already supplies its own create and drop SQL, leaving the standard exporter with no database-dependent behavior for a Dialect to customize.
replacement: Direct internal use of the standard AuxiliaryDatabaseObject-to-Exporter adapter
notes: No override and four schema-management consumers were observed; remove the redundant Dialect getter while preserving supported custom AuxiliaryDatabaseObject definitions and add a Migration Guide note.

rationale: The standard unique-key exporter is only an adapter which delegates every operation to the independently supplied UniqueDelegate.
replacement: getUniqueDelegate(), with an internal standard Exporter adapter
notes: No override and two schema-management consumers were observed; remove the duplicate supplier, route schema management through the standard adapter and supported UniqueDelegate, and add a versioned Migration Guide entry.

rationale: The CREATE INDEX command prefix is one part of the index-DDL rendering policy shared by the standard index exporter and unique-index delegate.
replacement: A supported composable IndexDdlSupport strategy supplied by the Dialect
notes: Seven overrides and two consumers were observed; preserve provider variation through the strategy, provide standard create and create-unique behavior, and add a versioned Migration Guide entry.

rationale: The index tail is a context-dependent rendering operation belonging with the create prefix and index-name qualification policy rather than directly on Dialect.
replacement: IndexDdlSupport renderCreateTail() using a focused immutable request exposing uniqueness and supported column views
notes: Eight overrides and one unique-index consumer were observed; replace the raw List<Column> signature with a focused supported request, preserve family composition, and test null-distinct and column-dependent variants.

rationale: Index-name qualification is an option of the same shared index-DDL policy used during both creation and removal.
replacement: IndexDdlSupport index-name qualification policy
notes: Eighteen overrides and four consumers were observed, including a community exporter; preserve provider USE through the strategy and test qualified and unqualified create and drop commands.

rationale: IF EXISTS placement for the target of ALTER TABLE is one context of a coherent DDL existence-check policy.
replacement: An immutable supported IfExistsSupport profile with ALTER_TABLE target placement
notes: Eleven overrides and one Dialect command-building consumer were observed; preserve provider configuration and add a versioned Migration Guide entry.

rationale: The before-table-name Boolean is mutually exclusive with the after-table-name Boolean and should be represented by one placement value.
replacement: IfExistsSupport DROP_TABLE placement using ExistenceCheckPlacement.NONE, BEFORE_NAME, or AFTER_NAME
notes: Twenty-three overrides and five consumers were observed, including provider delegation; preserve provider USE and test every placement without contradictory states.

rationale: The after-table-name Boolean is the alternate value of the same dropped-table existence-check placement.
replacement: IfExistsSupport DROP_TABLE placement AFTER_NAME
notes: Four overrides and two production consumers were observed; migrate H2 and HSQL family derivation to one explicit placement and reject contradictory configuration structurally.

rationale: The before-constraint-name Boolean is mutually exclusive with the after-constraint-name Boolean and is shared by unique and foreign-key removal.
replacement: IfExistsSupport DROP_CONSTRAINT placement using ExistenceCheckPlacement
notes: Thirteen overrides and three consumers were observed, including provider delegation; preserve use by UniqueDelegate and foreign-key exporters and test both constraint kinds.

rationale: The after-constraint-name Boolean is the alternate placement for the same DROP CONSTRAINT behavior.
replacement: IfExistsSupport DROP_CONSTRAINT placement AFTER_NAME
notes: No override and two consumers were observed; retain the supported possibility without a redundant independently configurable Boolean.

rationale: DROP INDEX existence-check placement belongs with table and constraint placement and should allow future after-name syntax without another Dialect method.
replacement: IfExistsSupport DROP_INDEX placement using ExistenceCheckPlacement
notes: Seven overrides and one unique-index-delegate consumer were observed; preserve provider configuration and test interaction with qualified index naming.

rationale: A Boolean cannot distinguish global constraint-check suspension from per-constraint disable and enable rendering, and currently permits missing command pairs.
replacement: A supported composable ConstraintControlSupport strategy with explicit NONE, GLOBAL, and PER_CONSTRAINT modes
notes: Nine overrides and two schema-truncation consumers were observed; derive availability from the selected mode, preserve provider configuration, and add a versioned Migration Guide entry.

rationale: The global disable statement is one half of GLOBAL constraint-control mode and is invalid without the corresponding enable statement.
replacement: ConstraintControlSupport GLOBAL mode disable command
notes: Four overrides and one standard-cleaner consumer were observed; require a paired enable command and test before-cleaning execution order.

rationale: The global enable statement is the closing half of GLOBAL constraint-control mode and should be configured atomically with disabling.
replacement: ConstraintControlSupport GLOBAL mode enable command
notes: Four overrides and one standard-cleaner consumer were observed; require a paired disable command and test after-cleaning execution even when appropriate failure handling is needed.

rationale: Per-constraint disable SQL is a rendering operation of PER_CONSTRAINT mode rather than an independently nullable Dialect method.
replacement: ConstraintControlSupport PER_CONSTRAINT renderer with a focused table-and-constraint request
notes: Five overrides and one standard-cleaner consumer were observed; replace positional String arguments with a supported immutable request and test quoted and qualified identifiers.

rationale: Per-constraint enable SQL is the paired rendering operation of PER_CONSTRAINT mode and must not be independently absent.
replacement: ConstraintControlSupport PER_CONSTRAINT enable renderer
notes: Five overrides and one standard-cleaner consumer were observed; require paired rendering behavior and test disable, truncate, and re-enable ordering.

rationale: Whether truncation accepts multiple table names is a mode of the truncate renderer and currently may disagree with the rendered statement list.
replacement: A supported composable TruncateSupport strategy with explicit PER_TABLE and MULTI_TABLE modes
notes: Four overrides and three consumers were observed; derive schema-truncation planning from the strategy mode, preserve provider configuration, and add a versioned Migration Guide entry.

rationale: Single-table truncate rendering is one operation of the coherent truncate strategy composed into the standard Cleaner family.
replacement: TruncateSupport rendering from a focused immutable table-name request
notes: Seven overrides and three provider or Dialect consumers were observed, including super-delegation; preserve reusable standard prefix and suffix composition and test qualified names.

rationale: Statement-list production is orchestration derived from truncate mode and rendering, not an independently overridable Dialect method.
replacement: TruncateSupport#renderStatements() returning an immutable ordered statement list
notes: No override and one standard-cleaner consumer were observed; replace the mutable array boundary, validate nonempty requests as appropriate, and test per-table ordering and multi-table joining.

rationale: Commands executed before schema-object removal are lifecycle orchestration and should support an ordered command list rather than one nullable Dialect string.
replacement: An immutable supported SchemaDropSupport profile containing ordered pre-drop commands
notes: Three PostgreSQL-family overrides and one schema-drop consumer were observed; preserve provider configuration, allow an empty immutable command list, and test execution before auxiliary objects, constraints, and tables.

rationale: Whether foreign keys and indexes are removed explicitly before tables is schema-drop planning policy consumed across the dropper and exporters.
replacement: SchemaDropSupport explicit dependent-object removal policy
notes: Twenty overrides and two consumers were observed; preserve storage-engine and family variation, clarify the foreign-key and index scope, and test explicit-removal and implicit-table-drop paths.

rationale: The deprecated complete-statement builder has no remaining caller or override and duplicates the retained table-exporter family plus IfExistsSupport and table-drop rendering composition.
replacement: getTableExporter() using supported table-drop composition and IfExistsSupport
notes: No override or consumer was observed; remove directly, preserve equivalent standard exporter behavior, and add a versioned Migration Guide entry.

rationale: The leading table-creation command is one part of table-definition rendering and should compose with the retained table exporter instead of remaining an isolated string hook on Dialect.
replacement: An immutable supported TableCreationSupport profile selecting the standard-table creation command
notes: Three overrides and five consumers were observed; preserve configuration-dependent HANA and SingleStore commands, migrate the persistent-temporary-table consumer, and test composition with explicit table types and the retained table-type suffix hook.

rationale: Multiset creation is a semantic variant of the table-creation command, including an explicit fallback to the standard command, rather than an independent Dialect concern.
replacement: TableCreationSupport command selection for STANDARD and MULTISET table semantics
notes: One Teradata override and one exporter consumer were observed; preserve the standard-command fallback and test primary-key-based selection without exposing exporter internals.

rationale: The cascade clause is table-drop rendering policy and belongs with the already-approved schema-drop composition rather than as a free-standing Dialect string hook.
replacement: SchemaDropSupport optional table-drop cascade clause
notes: Eighteen overrides and three consumers were observed; preserve the leading-space-independent rendering semantics, migrate the standard exporter, and test dialect-family variation with and without explicit dependent-object removal.

rationale: The complete ALTER TABLE prefix is shared rendering composition derived from the formatted table name and the already-approved existence-clause placement rather than an independently overridden Dialect method.
replacement: AlterTableSupport rendering from a focused table-name request composed with IfExistsSupport
notes: No override and six schema-management consumers were observed, including provider unique-key composition; expose supported composition without retaining a redundant Dialect string method and test qualified names with and without IF EXISTS.

rationale: The add-column prefix is one half of the database-specific column-addition grammar and should be represented together with its paired suffix in the table-alter family.
replacement: An immutable supported AlterTableSupport column-addition composition containing prefix and suffix
notes: Twelve overrides and two consumers were observed, including version-selected Teradata behavior; preserve configuration and family variation and test ADD COLUMN, ADD, and parenthesized forms.

rationale: The suffix has meaning only in combination with the add-column prefix and full rendered column declaration, so an independent override permits invalid pairings.
replacement: AlterTableSupport paired column-addition suffix
notes: Three overrides and one table-migrator consumer were observed; preserve HANA and Altibase paired parentheses and test the empty standard suffix.

rationale: Despite its name, this Boolean is consumed only as the availability gate for adding and dropping foreign-key constraints after table creation; it does not describe general ALTER TABLE support.
replacement: ForeignKeySupport explicit alter-table constraint availability
notes: Two community overrides and three schema-management consumers were observed; preserve the disabled IRIS and SQLite paths, remove the misleading general capability name, and test suppression of foreign-key export and migration.

rationale: The parallel arrays and Boolean encode a structured foreign-key definition through an error-prone positional contract and expose rendering as a fragment detached from its feature family.
replacement: ForeignKeySupport rendering from an immutable structured ForeignKeyConstraintRequest
notes: Ten overrides and three consumers were observed; the request carries the rendered constraint name, source columns, referenced table, target semantics, and target columns without parallel-array ambiguity, and tests preserve super-delegation and non-primary-key references.

rationale: A mapping-supplied foreign-key definition is an alternate input form for the same add-constraint operation, not a separate Dialect override contract.
replacement: ForeignKeyConstraintRequest optional explicit definition rendered by ForeignKeySupport
notes: Three community overrides and one exporter consumer were observed; use one request with mutually exclusive structured and explicit-definition forms, validate the shape, and test all existing custom-definition renderings.

rationale: The drop-constraint fragment is foreign-key DDL composition and should be rendered with its constraint name and existence-clause placement rather than exposed as a context-free string.
replacement: ForeignKeySupport drop rendering from a focused constraint request composed with AlterTableSupport and IfExistsSupport
notes: Five overrides and one exporter consumer were observed; preserve DROP CONSTRAINT and DROP FOREIGN KEY variants and test placement before and after the constraint name.

rationale: A single Boolean currently controls both schema rendering of every ON DELETE action and runtime reliance on database-side cascading, obscuring which action is supported.
replacement: ForeignKeySupport explicit support query for each OnDeleteAction
notes: Nine overrides and six schema or runtime consumers were observed; preserve existing all-or-none behavior as stock profiles while allowing action-specific capability, and test exporter rendering plus entity and collection cascade planning.

rationale: This runtime delete semantic belongs with foreign-key support and should state the required behavior rather than expose a historically named bug flag on Dialect.
replacement: ForeignKeySupport explicit self-referential delete behavior
notes: Four overrides and one runtime nullifier consumer were observed; preserve storage-engine-dependent MySQL behavior and test delete-time nullification for normal and affected databases.

rationale: The capability is never consumed, so retaining or relocating it would create an unsupported compatibility promise without affecting Hibernate behavior.
notes: Six overrides and no consumers were observed; remove the overrides and method directly and add a versioned Migration Guide entry.

rationale: Whether a logical unique key is represented as a constraint or unique index is selection policy already owned by the supplied UniqueDelegate family, not an independent Dialect Boolean.
replacement: A supported UniqueDelegate representation policy selecting a unique constraint or unique index for a focused request
notes: Two overrides and two metadata or delegate consumers were observed; preserve Spanner index selection and nullable-column fallback, and ensure metadata binding and DDL rendering consult the same policy.

rationale: NULLS NOT DISTINCT is a capability of unique-constraint rendering and should be declared by the strategy which renders the constraint.
replacement: UniqueDelegate family capability for NULLS NOT DISTINCT constraint semantics
notes: Three overrides and one delegate consumer were observed; preserve H2 and PostgreSQL support and test requested syntax for supporting and non-supporting delegates.

rationale: The context-free drop fragment leaks one implementation detail of the unique-key strategy while the supplied UniqueDelegate already owns the complete add and drop operation.
replacement: Supported UniqueDelegate request-based unique-key drop rendering composed with AlterTableSupport and IfExistsSupport
notes: Four overrides and one delegate consumer were observed; preserve DROP CONSTRAINT and DROP INDEX variants through supported delegate family bases or composition and test qualified names and existence-clause placement.

rationale: Whether partition-key columns must participate in primary keys is a focused database semantic consumed while building ordinary and temporal-table primary keys and is naturally implemented by provider Dialects.
notes: Five built-in overrides and two metadata consumers were observed; retain the focused hook instead of introducing a one-property support profile, preserve its incubating status as appropriate, and test ordinary and temporal history-table primary keys.

rationale: Hibernate never adds a primary key with ALTER TABLE, so the rendering hook and its provider overrides do not participate in any supported behavior.
notes: Five overrides and no consumers were observed; remove the method and overrides directly and add a versioned Migration Guide entry.

rationale: A Boolean for all column checks cannot express the distinct anonymous and named placement rules and must be interpreted together with two other capability methods.
replacement: CheckConstraintSupport explicit supported placements including ANONYMOUS_COLUMN and NAMED_COLUMN
notes: Twelve overrides and four metadata or exporter consumers were observed; migrate placement as one profile, validate that named-column support implies column support, and test inline rendering and table-level hoisting.

rationale: Named-column support is a subtype of check-constraint placement and its default delegation to column support permits capability combinations which consumers must reconstruct procedurally.
replacement: CheckConstraintSupport NAMED_COLUMN placement capability
notes: Three overrides and two DDL consumers were observed; preserve Informix and MariaDB behavior and test selection of the first named column constraint versus table-level rendering.

rationale: Table-level support is the third coupled placement decision and should be selected from the same immutable constraint profile.
replacement: CheckConstraintSupport TABLE placement capability
notes: Four community overrides and four metadata or exporter consumers were observed; preserve unsupported databases and temporal-table behavior and test column-check hoisting only when table placement is available.

rationale: Rendering currently accepts a mutable mapping object and delegates part of the grammar to a second string-rewriting hook, coupling supported provider behavior to mapping internals and call order.
replacement: CheckConstraintSupport rendering from an immutable CheckConstraintRenderRequest containing placement, optional name, expression, and options
notes: Three overrides and one mapping consumer were observed; preserve standard, Informix, and SQL Server grammar while removing CheckConstraint#constraintString(Dialect) coupling and test anonymous, named, column, and table forms.

rationale: Appending options to already-rendered SQL cannot represent dialects which place options before the expression and exposes an internal two-stage rendering protocol.
replacement: Single CheckConstraintSupport render operation over CheckConstraintRenderRequest
notes: Six overrides and four renderer consumers were observed; preserve before-expression and trailing option placement through one strategy and test empty and nonempty options without exposing partially rendered SQL.

rationale: The no-argument nullable-column fragment exists only as a fallback for the type-aware overload, requiring providers to choose between two overlapping override points.
replacement: ColumnDefinitionSupport nullable-column rendering from a type-aware immutable request
notes: Six overrides and one delegating consumer were observed; migrate generic fragments as the default type-independent strategy and test empty, NULL, and database-specific nullable clauses.

rationale: Nullable syntax can depend on the SQL type, but the raw string overload is one part of the larger column-definition grammar and duplicates the no-argument fallback contract.
replacement: ColumnDefinitionSupport single nullable-column renderer receiving the rendered SQL type
notes: Three overrides and five consumers were observed; preserve MySQL and SingleStore TIMESTAMP behavior, migrate temporary-table rendering, and test type-sensitive fallback without super-method coupling.

rationale: Default-expression normalization is column-definition rendering behavior and must compose with nullability and generated-column clause ordering.
replacement: ColumnDefinitionSupport default-expression renderer
notes: One Spanner override and one DDL consumer were observed; preserve conditional parenthesization and test already-parenthesized and unparenthesized expressions.

rationale: Generated-column clause rendering is coupled to type presence and nullability placement and should not remain a free-standing Dialect string hook.
replacement: ColumnDefinitionSupport generated-expression renderer composed with generated-column ordering policy
notes: Fifteen overrides and four consumers were observed; preserve standard, stored, virtual, computed, and version-dependent forms and test provider delegation through supported family composition.

rationale: A Boolean ordering exception is meaningful only while composing default, generated, and nullability fragments and permits consumers to reconstruct an incomplete grammar.
replacement: ColumnDefinitionSupport explicit clause-order policy for nullability, default, and generated clauses
notes: One Spanner override and one DDL consumer were observed; preserve NOT NULL before DEFAULT and test standard and Spanner orderings as complete column definitions.

rationale: Whether nullability may follow a generated clause is another generated-column ordering rule and should be represented alongside type presence and clause order.
replacement: ColumnDefinitionSupport generated-column nullability policy
notes: Four overrides and one DDL consumer were observed; preserve DB2, MariaDB, PostgreSQL, and Spanner omission behavior and test nullable and non-null generated columns.

rationale: A single Boolean cannot represent independent local, global, and persistent temporary-table strategies and is already superseded by strategy presence.
replacement: Non-null getLocalTemporaryTableStrategy(), getGlobalTemporaryTableStrategy(), or getPersistentTemporaryTableStrategy() results
notes: Deprecated for removal since 7.1 with two community overrides and no consumers; remove directly, migrate capability assertions to strategy presence, and add a versioned Migration Guide entry.

rationale: Primary-key support varies by temporary-table kind and is already a capability of the selected TemporaryTableStrategy.
replacement: TemporaryTableStrategy#supportsTemporaryTablePrimaryKey()
notes: Deprecated for removal since 7.1 with three community overrides and one legacy-strategy consumer; migrate the overrides into the corresponding strategies and add a versioned Migration Guide entry.

rationale: The create command is strategy-specific and the Dialect method exists only for the deprecated legacy adapter.
replacement: TemporaryTableStrategy#getTemporaryTableCreateCommand()
notes: Deprecated for removal since 7.1 with thirteen overrides and two legacy consumers; migrate all provider behavior to local, global, or persistent strategies and test each selected kind.

rationale: Create options depend on the selected temporary-table kind and are already supplied by TemporaryTableStrategy.
replacement: TemporaryTableStrategy#getTemporaryTableCreateOptions()
notes: Deprecated for removal since 7.1 with thirteen overrides and two legacy consumers; preserve nullable no-options semantics, migrate family strategies, and add a versioned Migration Guide entry.

rationale: The drop command belongs to the selected lifecycle strategy and the Dialect hook only supports the obsolete legacy path.
replacement: TemporaryTableStrategy#getTemporaryTableDropCommand()
notes: Deprecated for removal since 7.1 with four overrides and two legacy consumers; preserve DROP TABLE and database-specific variants through strategy tests and Migration Guide guidance.

rationale: Cleanup rendering varies by temporary-table strategy and already has a strategy-owned contract.
replacement: TemporaryTableStrategy#getTemporaryTableTruncateCommand()
notes: Deprecated for removal since 7.1 with two HANA overrides and two legacy consumers; preserve DELETE FROM and TRUNCATE variants through the HANA global strategy and add migration guidance.

rationale: Per-column temporary-table annotations depend on the selected strategy and are already rendered through its type-aware method.
replacement: TemporaryTableStrategy#getCreateTemporaryTableColumnAnnotation(int)
notes: Deprecated for removal since 7.1 with two SQL Server overrides and one legacy consumer; migrate COLLATE DATABASE_DEFAULT behavior and test relevant SQL type codes.

rationale: After-use lifecycle is strategy-specific and the Dialect method cannot describe different actions for multiple supported table kinds.
replacement: TemporaryTableStrategy#getTemporaryTableAfterUseAction()
notes: Deprecated for removal since 7.1 with nine overrides and one legacy consumer; migrate CLEAN, DROP, and NONE behavior to the corresponding strategies and add a versioned Migration Guide entry.

rationale: Before-use lifecycle is strategy-specific and already participates directly in temporary-table execution through TemporaryTableStrategy.
replacement: TemporaryTableStrategy#getTemporaryTableBeforeUseAction()
notes: Deprecated for removal since 7.1 with twelve overrides and one legacy consumer; migrate CLEAN and NONE behavior, remove LegacyTemporaryTableStrategy, and test execution lifecycle ordering.

rationale: A global Boolean for standalone COMMENT ON syntax must be combined with empty-string probes of two inline-rendering hooks to determine the actual comment path.
replacement: A supported CommentSupport strategy selecting NONE, INLINE, or STATEMENT placement per schema-object target
notes: Twenty-two overrides and two exporter consumers were observed; represent table, column, and user-defined-type targets explicitly and test standalone, inline, and unsupported paths without sentinel-string probing.

rationale: An empty inline fragment currently doubles as a signal to generate a standalone statement, coupling rendering and capability through string inspection.
replacement: CommentSupport rendering from an immutable table CommentRequest according to explicit placement
notes: Five overrides and two table-exporter consumers were observed; preserve HANA, MySQL, and SingleStore inline syntax and test coexistence with table type/options suffixes.

rationale: Column-comment placement and rendering are part of the same target-aware comment feature and should not be exposed as a second sentinel-returning Dialect method.
replacement: CommentSupport rendering from an immutable column CommentRequest according to explicit placement
notes: Five overrides and two DDL consumers were observed; preserve inline column comments and qualified standalone COMMENT ON COLUMN commands and test escaping and absent comments.

rationale: The deprecated capability has no override or consumer and therefore describes no Hibernate or provider behavior.
notes: Deprecated for removal since 7.1 with no observed usage; remove directly and add a versioned Migration Guide entry.

rationale: Provider Dialects must sometimes normalize or refine JDBC metadata before the version is captured, existing implementations legitimately delegate to the standard resolution behavior, and integration providers may invoke the selected Dialect's version-resolution behavior outside subclass context.
notes: Nine overrides, two constructor or super-delegation consumers, and an integration-provider use case were observed; retain public visibility for provider USE, document invocation during superclass construction for IMPLEMENT, require a supported DialectResolutionInfo signature, and test defaulting and vendor-specific parsing. Public SPI visibility does not make the method application API.

rationale: The immutable version selected during construction is heavily consumed by provider Dialects, translators, and Hibernate feature selection, but overriding the accessor can contradict the captured constructor state.
notes: Two overrides and 415 consumers were observed; make the accessor final, migrate MimerSQL and RDMS OS 2200 to establish their effective version during construction, and retain DatabaseVersion as supported USE SPI.

rationale: Minimum-version validation is fixed constructor orchestration with no override and should not expose a protected lifecycle hook invoked before subclass construction completes.
replacement: Private constructor validation using the captured version and getMinimumSupportedVersion()
notes: No override and two constructor consumers were observed; the overridable method boundary was removed, warning behavior was preserved, and explicit versions below and at the minimum remain tested.

rationale: The diagnostic representation of a Dialect and its captured version is useful supported behavior, but provider-specific overriding would weaken predictable diagnostics without an observed extension need.
notes: No override or indexed consumer was observed; retain the class-and-version representation and make the method final so it is not part of the IMPLEMENT surface.

rationale: Whether JDBC cross-reference metadata supplements imported keys is extraction strategy configuration and should not require the standard extractor to call back into Dialect.
replacement: A supported InformationExtractor foreign-key metadata policy selecting IMPORTED_KEYS_ONLY or IMPORTED_KEYS_AND_CROSS_REFERENCE
notes: One Informix override and one standard-extractor consumer were observed; migrate the behavior into supported JDBC metadata extractor composition and test merging without duplicate foreign keys.

rationale: The optional parent-table filter is meaningful only for cross-reference retrieval and can form an invalid combination when exposed independently from its enabling Boolean.
replacement: The optional parent-table filter in the InformationExtractor cross-reference policy
notes: One Informix override and one extractor consumer were observed; require the filter only for the cross-reference mode, preserve null and wildcard semantics, and test the exact DatabaseMetaData#getCrossReference arguments.

rationale: A nullable string simultaneously signals row-id availability, chooses a default pseudo-column, and resolves an optional mapping-supplied name, while its type and DDL declaration live in separate hooks.
replacement: A supported RowIdSupport profile resolving a locator expression from an immutable optional-name request
notes: Twelve overrides and nine consumers were observed; provide an explicit unsupported profile instead of null capability probing and test fixed pseudo-columns, supplied names, defaults, and deliberately disabled inherited support.

rationale: The optional physical declaration is meaningful only for a supported row-id locator and currently calls back into the independent expression hook.
replacement: RowIdSupport optional physical column declaration composed from the same locator request
notes: Three DB2-family overrides and one table-exporter consumer were observed; preserve implicit pseudo-columns and explicit generated ROWID declarations and test consistency with the resolved expression and locator type.

rationale: Empty-string/null equivalence is database value semantics used by cast emulation and is clearer as an explicit semantic choice than a negatively contextual Boolean hook.
replacement: A supported StringValueSemantics profile with DISTINCT and AS_NULL empty-string semantics
notes: Five overrides and one cast-function consumer were observed; preserve Oracle, Postgres Plus, and TimesTen behavior and test array-to-string casting for both semantic modes.

rationale: Fixed-length CHAR trailing-space behavior is another database string-value semantic and should be represented alongside empty-string treatment.
replacement: StringValueSemantics with PRESERVED and STRIPPED fixed-length trailing-space semantics
notes: Three overrides and one CharacterJavaType consumer were observed; preserve MySQL and Sybase wrapping behavior and test single-character values containing only spaces.

rationale: Whether concatenation accepts non-string arguments is function grammar and coercion policy already in the scope of FunctionSyntaxSupport.
replacement: FunctionSyntaxSupport concatenation-argument coercion policy
notes: Five overrides and one SQL AST translator consumer were observed; preserve DB2, Derby, and Transact-SQL casts and test equality-preserving row-component concatenation.

rationale: The required cast around integer division is a focused function-expression coercion rule, not a general standalone Dialect capability.
replacement: FunctionSyntaxSupport integer-division result coercion policy
notes: Three overrides and one extract-function consumer were observed; preserve HSQL and IRIS week extraction and test casted versus direct integer division rendering.

rationale: No Hibernate code consults this cast-truncation capability, so its three overrides do not select any observable behavior.
notes: Three overrides and no consumers were observed; remove the method and overrides directly and add a versioned Migration Guide entry.

rationale: Provider Dialects may need to select column-label or column-name extraction to account for JDBC driver behavior, and the existing focused strategy is an appropriate supported extension contract.
notes: No in-repository override and one runtime consumer were observed; retain ColumnAliasExtractor and its standard label and name strategies as supported SPI and cover both choices in the compatibility test kit.

rationale: The optional default ordinality-column name is set-returning-function syntax capability and should be represented with the rest of the function grammar instead of as a nullable standalone Dialect hook.
replacement: FunctionSyntaxSupport explicit optional default ordinality-column name
notes: Nine overrides and two consumers were observed; preserve the family-specific names and explicit unsupported state and test both type resolution and SQL rendering.

rationale: A provider Dialect supplies a coherent row-level-security strategy used during boot and runtime, making the existing strategy boundary a natural supported extension contract.
notes: Five overrides and two consumers were observed; classify RowLevelSecurity, its tenant-identifier source, and stock unsupported behavior consistently as SPI and test provider selection and runtime use.

rationale: The hook exists only to support the deprecated legacy GUIDGenerator and should not remain in the Dialect extension surface after that generator is removed.
replacement: UuidGenerator
notes: Thirteen overrides and two calls, including one superclass delegation, were observed; remove the legacy generator, method, and overrides and add a versioned Migration Guide entry directing users to UuidGenerator.

rationale: The deprecated protected method is an unoverridden wrapper around the supported timeout conversion utility and provides no Dialect-specific behavior.
replacement: Timeouts#getTimeoutInSeconds(int)
notes: No override and four provider-internal consumers were observed; migrate those consumers to Timeouts and add a versioned Migration Guide entry for removal of the protected hook.

rationale: Whether CREATE VIEW requires an explicit column list is a genuine focused grammar variation, while introducing a one-property strategy profile would add indirection without improving composition.
notes: One Informix override and one table-exporter consumer were observed; retain the Boolean hook as supported SPI and test both explicit-column-list and standard rendering.
